draft.title: Stocktakes and inventory losses
card: A stocktake is a physical count of the inventory a business has on hand. The count is compared with the quantity shown in the inventory records.
the count is lower than the records. Causes include theft, damage and goods going out of date.
the count is higher than the records. A common cause is an error, such as goods received but not recorded.
The records are then adjusted to match the count. The count is used because it shows what the business actually holds.
draft.remember: Count the stock, compare it with the records, then adjust the records to match the count.

a.q: A stocktake finds fewer units than the inventory records show. What does this difference show?
opts: An inventory loss, so the records are adjusted down
An inventory gain, so the records are adjusted down
An inventory loss, so the count is adjusted up
An inventory gain, so the count is adjusted up
a.why: A count below the records means stock is missing, which is an inventory loss. The records are adjusted to match the physical count, so they go down. The count is not changed, because it shows what is really there.
a.clue: Which is lower, the count or the records?

b.q: Mia's gift shop in Ballarat has 40 vases in its records. A stocktake finds 43 on the shelves. A delivery of 3 vases was never entered. What should Mia do?
opts: Record an inventory gain and adjust the records up to 43
Record an inventory loss and adjust the records down to 37
Leave the records at 40 and treat 3 vases as spare
Adjust the count down to 40 to match the records
b.why: The count is higher than the records, so there is an inventory gain caused by an error. The records are adjusted up to 43 to match what is held. Keeping 40 is wrong because the records must follow the physical count.
b.clue: Which is higher, the count or the records, and which one is trusted?

a.best: An inventory loss, so the records are adjusted down

b.best: Record an inventory gain and adjust the records up to 43
